Quote source · Q0102

Who said “What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee”?

The located source for this passage, the original-language wording where one exists, and the forms of it that circulate without the attribution.

Quote source / Marcus Aurelius / What is not good for…

English

What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.
Thinker Marcus Aurelius
Work Meditations VI.54
School Stoicism
Theme Community

Checked against the cited edition on 2026-09-14.

The recorded source

Attributed to
Marcus Aurelius
Work and locator
Meditations VI.54
English wording
“What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.”
Original wording (Ancient Greek)
τὸ τῇ μέλισσῃ μὴ συμφέρον οὐδὲ τῷ συμμέλει συμφέρει.

The Greek second noun is συμμέλει, the swarm. The standard English rendering says “hive,” which names the structure rather than the colony.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a Koine Greek source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

The wording recorded here is the one this archive holds. These are the forms that circulate in its place:

  • “What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.”
  • “What is not beneficial to the swarm is not beneficial to the bee.”
  • “What is not good for the swarm is not good for the bee.”

Attribution notes

Meditations VI.54, where the sentence belongs to Marcus Aurelius' argument that he was made for the whole and cannot act against it. The image is a swarm — a body that the individual bee physically cannot survive leaving — and the popular English substitution of “hive” bends it toward a claim about institutions and conformity, which is the opposite of the Stoic point about natural membership.

What is the exact wording of the quotation from Marcus Aurelius?

The wording recorded here is: “What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.” The Ancient Greek reads: τὸ τῇ μέλισσῃ μὴ συμφέρον οὐδὲ τῷ συμμέλει συμφέρει. The Greek second noun is συμμέλει, the swarm. The standard English rendering says “hive,” which names the structure rather than the colony. Forms in circulation that differ from this wording: What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee. / What is not beneficial to the swarm is not beneficial to the bee. / What is not good for the swarm is not good for the bee.
